181.synopsis:
Wang Lin was a bright and kindhearted boy raised by loving parents. Despite being shunned by their relatives, his parents always held hope that their son would rise above and achieve greatness. When an opportunity to pursue immortality finally came, Wang Lin eagerly stepped onto the path of cultivation—only to discover that his talent was mediocre at best.
But this is not a tale of natural-born genius.
Through unyielding determination, sharp wit, and sheer willpower, Wang Lin embarks on a relentless journey to overcome his limitations. Along the way, he faces brutal enemies, makes powerful allies, and slowly transforms from a naive youth into a ruthless, cunning cultivator who defies both heaven and fate itself.
In a world where strength dictates survival, and immortality is a distant dream for most, Wang Lin perseveres, fueled by determination and wisdom. As he navigates the treacherous path of cultivation, his journey inspires both awe and respect, leaving behind a legacy that will not easily be forgotten.

‘I wonder what kind of expression he’s making….’
He wondered why he’d stopped him with such a voice full of despair.
The force gripping Ju-eon’s wrist was so sorrowful and desperate that, even though he could easily shake it off, Ju-eon couldn’t. As he blinked quickly, his eyes adjusted to the darkness and took in the man’s face. For a moment, he forgot to breathe.
The grown man was crying. Ju-eon’s eyes widened at the tears flowing like silence. His eyes grew hot, perhaps from not blinking for so long. The man stepped back. This time, Ju-eon took a step forward.
“Um… why are you crying…”
He didn’t think he was foolish enough to care about the actions of someone who was drunk, but his heart sank. The man cried silently. His voice, wet and low, clung to Ju-eon’s heart. Ju-eon suddenly caught a sense of foreboding.
“I waited nicely.”
A boiling emotion could be felt in his deeply sunken voice. A premonition that his voice, now stuck to his heart, wouldn’t detach for a long time.
“Hey. What does that even mean…”
Despite Ju-eon’s call, the man continued to say only what he wanted to say. The man whispered incomprehensible words without pause.
“Don’t go today.”
Every day, I just stood far enough away not to touch you.
At the desperate voice, Ju-eon forgot even to hold his breath for a moment. With each blink, the outline of the face became clearer and clearer in his vision. Logically thinking, even though he knew the probability of this man being drunk and mistaking him for someone else was higher than him being someone he knew.
“I think you’re mistaking me for someone else.”
“…Eon-ah.”

106677.synopsis:
Zero Compatibility. 
A Guide in Name Only—Practically an Ordinary Person.  
As an F-Guide with almost no chance of matching with an Esper, Ben had always believed he could continue living his uneventful, unremarkable life.  
Until he met that man.  
“Found you. My Guide.”  
The sudden appearance of Haimar, a monstrous Esper who boldly declared Ben as his Guide, shattered everything Ben thought he knew. 
With him came a shocking revelation about Ben’s own rank—one that turned his quiet life upside down.  
Swept into an unrelenting series of events, the two are drawn together, their bodies and hearts inching ever closer…  
* * *  
Physical contact between two complete strangers—how was that even possible? 
At least within Ben’s understanding of common sense, it wasn’t.  
“Uh, I still don’t even know if I’m really your Guide…”  
Zing.  
The sharp blue eyes staring into his made his headache flare up again, as if it had only been momentarily subdued.  
Still, it wasn’t as bad as back in the container, so Ben chose to buy time by voicing his honest uncertainty. 
After all, the one most affected by this connection was the Esper. 
Guides, strictly speaking, could live perfectly fine without an Esper.

“Want to check?”  
Wait—hold on. 
Why was he coming closer?!  
Before Ben could react, Haimar, with a face annoyingly sculpted to perfection, took Ben’s hand and placed it against his cheek.  
Smooth, flawless skin brushed against his palm. 
And before he could pull away, his fingers grazed something even warmer—Haimar’s lips.  
The contrast between his cool skin and the heat of his breath sent an odd shiver down Ben’s spine. 
He instinctively tried to twist his hand away, but his fingers, caught in an iron grip, instead trailed across the Esper’s ear.  
That’s when he noticed them—three thick, metallic piercings: a rugged hoop and two circular studs.  
Those weren’t just accessories.  
They were control devices, temporary stabilizers used by high-ranking Espers when their abilities became unstable or when they required emotional regulation.  
But having three at once?  
Ben froze.  
His stunned expression didn’t go unnoticed. 
Haimar, still holding his hand, intertwined their fingers with an easy familiarity, his long fingers wrapping around Ben’s.  
“If I hold you,” he murmured, voice low and dangerous, “I think we’ll both find out for sure.”
